title: Counterdiabatic Quantum Circuits
authors: Ankit Wenju Shrestha, Budhaditya Bhattacharjee, Adolfo del Campo
abstract: Counterdiabatic driving provides a universal route to fast quantum control, but its standard formulation presupposes a Hamiltonian generator. We develop a Hamiltonian-free theory of the adiabatic gauge potential (AGP) for parameter-dependent unitary operators $U_λ$. Exact and regularized versions of the AGP follow from a Hermitian, banded linear system at a cost comparable to the Lanczos construction in the Hermitian case, requiring neither diagonalization nor a matrix logarithm. We demonstrate rapid convergence of the truncated Krylov approximation for the kicked top and for an integrable brickwork circuit built from unitary $\check{R}$ matrices, a setting in which no local effective Hamiltonian is available. Our results extend shortcuts to adiabaticity, and AGP-based diagnostics of chaos, to Floquet systems and quantum circuits.
summary: This paper introduces a novel, Hamiltonian-free framework to calculate the Adiabatic Gauge Potential (AGP) for quantum systems evolving via unitary gates. By utilizing the Krylov space method, the authors provide an efficient way to calculate this potential for complex quantum circuits and Floquet systems. This allows for robust diagnostics of quantum chaos and the design of faster, more robust quantum control protocols.
main_problem: The paper develops a Hamiltonian-free theory for the Adiabatic Gauge Potential (AGP) to enable fast quantum control in systems governed by unitary operators.
main_result: The AGP can be calculated directly from the unitary operator and its derivative, bypassing the need for an explicit Hamiltonian, and this method is applicable to quantum circuits and Floquet systems.
method: The authors use a superoperator formulation and the Krylov space method to derive and approximate the AGP, avoiding computationally intensive steps like diagonalization or matrix logarithms.
model_or_system: The theory is applied to general unitary operators $U_\lambda$, specifically demonstrated on the quantum kicked top and the brickwork circuit, which models dynamics via local unitary gates.
key_observables: Adiabatic Gauge Potential (AGP), AGP Norm ($\|A_\lambda\|$), and infidelity ($1-F$).
important_parameters: The parameter $\lambda$ governing the unitary evolution, and the regularization parameter $\eta$ used for numerical stability.
main_assumptions: The standard AGP formulation is extended to unitary systems, and the Krylov approximation is used to truncate the infinite series expansion.
figures_summary: Figures compare the AGP norm scaling to chaos indicators (like mean level spacing ratio) for the kicked top, and show the monotonic convergence of the approximate AGP norm to the true value.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the Hamiltonian-free AGP theory, then applies it to specific unitary models like the kicked top and brickwork circuit, detailing the mathematical machinery (Krylov/CMV basis) at each step.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, general diagnostic tool (AGP) for characterizing quantum chaos and optimizing quantum gates in circuit models, which is highly relevant for quantum computation.
